title: FBI Assisting After Suspicious Package Sent to Cuellar's Laredo Office on Election Day
excerpt: A suspicious package delivered to U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar's Laredo district office on Election Day morning prompted an evacuation, a hazmat response and a…
content:
A suspicious package delivered to U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar's district office in Laredo on Election Day morning prompted an evacuation, a hazardous-materials response and a precautionary health screening for one staff member, and the FBI is now assisting in the investigation, according to KGNS.

Laredo police and hazmat crews responded to the East Calton Road plaza around 11:30 a.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 3, after the package was reported, according to KGNS.

One staff member was sent for a precautionary health screening. The staffer who opened the package is the one who was screened, according to KGNS.

Cuellar's campaign manager, Max Scher, confirmed the FBI's involvement and said, "All members of Team Cuellar are safely accounted for," according to KGNS.

"Violence has no place in politics. Intimidation has no place in politics," Scher said, according to KGNS.

What remains unknown

Authorities have not released details on the package's contents, and the investigation remains ongoing, according to KGNS. That leaves the central questions unanswered four days later: what was inside the package, whether it was dangerous, and whether it was meant as a threat.

The timing adds to the concern. The package arrived on the morning of a midterm Election Day, while voters across Webb County were casting ballots in races including the mayoral contest and the TX-28 congressional race Cuellar had just won. No official has said the package was connected to the election, and no suspect or motive has been publicly identified.

Webb Watch 956 will continue to follow this story and will update it when the FBI or Laredo police release findings on the package's contents or any charges.
